title: Wipe the used oil off a removed piston whose connecting rod swings
instruction: Clean the oil off the outside of the piston.
context: Done by: automotive service technicians and mechanics (O*NET 49-3023; 825,800 US jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook), whose O*NET tasks include "Repair or replace parts such as pistons, rods, gears, valves, and bearings" and "Disassemble units and inspect parts for wear". Before a piston is inspected for scoring and wear, used oil is cleaned off with solvent and no wire brush may touch it (GM piston cleaning and inspection procedure, third-party copy; Detroit Diesel Series 60 manual 1.19.3.1, third-party copy). This is the bench wipe-down before a visual check, not the full wash before reassembly. Left alone, the heavy rod tips the assembly over; a loaded sponge smears oil until it is rinsed with agitation.
setup: Station table. Rubber bench mat 30 x 30 x 0.4 cm, fixed, centre (0.30, -0.02). On it: a 1.6 L car-engine piston (cast aluminium, 75 mm dia x 50 mm, compression height 30 mm, dished crown, 3 ring grooves, hollow skirt; 300 g with its 19 mm steel wrist pin) standing crown down at (0.30, 0.02), its forged-steel connecting rod (137 mm centre to centre, I-beam, 470 g) on the pin, free to swing +-44.8 deg until the beam meets the skirt edge; at the start the rod tips over and the assembly lies on the mat. Left of the mat: a parts sponge on a stick (polyurethane foam 4 x 4 x 4 cm, 3 g, glued under the end of a 20 x 1.6 x 1.6 cm wooden handle, 25 g; handle end on a 3 x 3 x 2.4 cm block) at (0.33, 0.30), and a steel tray of parts-washer solvent, 20 x 15 x 4 cm inside, 3 cm of solvent, fixed, centre (0.46, 0.215). Right of the mat: a flat foam sponge 8 x 8 x 2 cm, 6 g, at (0.24, -0.26). Positions in metres, world frame of the station (x away from the arms, y left).
scoring: Used oil carries a UV tracer. The piston's outside is divided into 145 cells of about 1 cm: 100 on the skirt below the ring belt (ring grooves excluded) and 45 on the crown including its dish. A cell counts as clean once the pressed sponge has been moved at least 3 cm across it; in a real trial, count cells still glowing under a UV torch on four side photos and one crown photo through a printed grid. 0.25 at 25% of cells clean, 0.5 at 50%, 0.75 at 75%, 1.0 at 95% or more with the piston and its rod both lying still on the mat, released (otherwise 0.75). 0 if at any time the piston falls more than 3 cm (vertical speed above 0.77 m/s) or is put into the solvent, or if it ends off the mat. Inside of the skirt and the rod are not scored.
reset_notes: Re-apply a fixed amount of dyed oil with a brush; replace both sponges and the solvent.
fidelity: Oil is a per-cell state: a cell clears after the sponge, pressed so its 3 cm core touches, slides 3 cm over it; 5 mm of foam conforms to curvature. The sponge holds 60 cells, then smears; it unloads 1 cell per mm moved in solvent. Solvent is not a fluid. Colliders are simple shapes with the real sizes; the piston and rod meshes are visual. Sponges are rigid cores, not deformable.
